Find the area $A$ bounded by the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

When $r(\theta )=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(9{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4+5{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(4+\frac{5(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))}{2}+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{13}{2}-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{13}{2}\theta -\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{13\pi }{4}+6) \\  & =3+\frac{13\pi }{8} \\  & =\frac{13\pi +24}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
